source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Public 20:45–49 = Hebrew 21:1–5; public 21:1–32 = Hebrew 21:6–37. All other selected labels match. Complete original records, including annotations, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps the unexplained thirtieth year and the exile setting before the vision.
verses.before: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the Chebar canal, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
verses.after: In the thirtieth year, on the fifth day of the fourth month, I was among the exiles beside the Kebar River. The heavens opened, and I saw visions of God.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was among the exiles by the Chebar canal, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.

verses.rationale: Retains the second dating formula rather than merging it into the first.
verses.before: On the fifth day of the month, it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,
verses.after: It was the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of King Jehoiachin’s exile.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the fifth day of the month, it was the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,

verses.rationale: Preserves the third-person introduction and the hand image.
verses.before: the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel the son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Chebar canal, and there the hand of the LORD was upon him.
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Ezekiel the priest, son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans beside the Kebar River. There the hand of the LORD came upon him.
verses.tsw_comparator: the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel the son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans by the Chebar canal, and there the hand of the LORD was upon him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the layered location and uncertain metal comparison.
verses.before: I looked, and look, a stormy wind came from the north, a great cloud with a brightness around it, and fire flashing forth continually, and among the fire was something like gleaming metal.
verses.after: I looked: a storm wind was coming from the north, a great cloud with fire flashing within it and brightness all around. At its center, within the fire, something gleamed like glowing metal.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked, and behold, a stormy wind came from the north, a great cloud with a brightness around it, and fire flashing forth continually, and in the midst of the fire was something like gleaming metal.

verses.rationale: Repeated likeness makes the description analogical rather than a literal identification.
verses.before: From within it came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had a human likeness,
verses.after: Within it was the likeness of four living creatures. This is how they appeared: they had a human likeness,
verses.tsw_comparator: From within it came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance: they had a human likeness,

verses.rationale: Carries the surprising qualification across the verse boundary.
verses.before: but each had four faces, and each of them had four wings.
verses.after: but each had four faces and four wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: but each had four faces, and each of them had four wings.

verses.rationale: Preserves calf feet and the bronze comparison without modern machinery imagery.
verses.before: Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like burnished bronze.
verses.after: Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the soles of a calf’s feet. They sparkled like polished bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot, and they sparkled like burnished bronze.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form hands while retaining the concluding summary.
verses.before: Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. And the four had their faces and their wings thus:
verses.after: They had human hands beneath their wings on all four sides. All four had faces and wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. And the four had their faces and their wings thus:

verses.rationale: Makes movement intelligible while keeping the repeated no-turning detail.
verses.before: their wings touched one another. Each one of them went straight forward, not turning as they went.
verses.after: Their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they moved; each went straight ahead.
verses.tsw_comparator: their wings touched one another. Each one of them went straight forward, not turning as they went.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four faces and the two specified directions.
verses.before: As for the likeness of their faces, each had the face of a human, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left, and the face of an eagle for each.
verses.after: As for their faces, all four had a human face, a lion’s face on the right, an ox’s face on the left, and an eagle’s face.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the likeness of their faces, each had the face of a human, the face of a lion on the right, the face of an ox on the left, and the face of an eagle for each.

verses.rationale: Separates the face summary from the wing arrangement without adding a direction for the eagle.
verses.before: Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above; each creature had two wings touching the wing of another, while two covered their bodies.
verses.after: Such were their faces. Their wings spread upward; each had two wings touching another creature’s wings and two covering its body.
verses.tsw_comparator: Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above; each creature had two wings touching the wing of another, while two covered their bodies.

verses.rationale: Keeps spirit and the guiding relation open without replacing it with instinct.
verses.before: And each person went straight forward; wherever the spirit was to go, they went, not turning as they went.
verses.after: Each went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went, without turning as they moved.
verses.tsw_comparator: And each one went straight forward; wherever the spirit was to go, they went, not turning as they went.

verses.rationale: Retains both the creatures’ appearance and fire among them despite the compressed syntax.
verses.before: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches moving to and fro among the living creatures. And the fire was bright, and from the fire went forth lightning.
verses.after: The living creatures looked like burning coals of fire, like torches. Fire moved back and forth among the creatures; it shone brightly, and lightning flashed from it.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches moving to and fro among the living creatures. And the fire was bright, and from the fire went forth lightning.

verses.rationale: Renders rapid movement without identifying its mechanism.
verses.before: And the living creatures darted back and forth, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
verses.after: The creatures darted back and forth like flashes of lightning.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the living creatures darted back and forth, like the appearance of a flash of lightning.

verses.rationale: Distributes the singular wheel naturally across the four creatures; note records compressed Hebrew.
verses.before: Now as I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the earth beside each living creature, one for each of the four of them.
verses.after: As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside each of the four-faced creatures.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now as I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the earth beside each living creature, one for each of the four of them.

verses.rationale: Keeps mineral identification provisional and the wheel-within-wheel image.
verses.before: As for the appearance of the wheels and their construction, their appearance was like the gleaming of beryl. And the four had the same likeness, their construction being like a wheel within a wheel.
verses.after: The wheels and their workmanship gleamed like beryl. All four had the same likeness, and each looked as though one wheel were set within another.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the appearance of the wheels and their construction, their appearance was like the gleaming of beryl. And the four had the same likeness, their construction being like a wheel within a wheel.

verses.rationale: Preserves four directions and the refrain.
verses.before: When they went, they went in any one of their four directions without turning as they went.
verses.after: They could move in any of their four directions without turning as they went.
verses.tsw_comparator: When they went, they went in any one of their four directions without turning as they went.

verses.rationale: Retains eyes rather than interpreting them as decorations.
verses.before: Their rims were high and fearsome, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.
verses.after: Their rims were high and awe-inspiring, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their rims were high and fearsome, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.

verses.rationale: Makes the synchronized motions explicit without reducing the repetition.
verses.before: When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.
verses.after: When the living creatures moved, the wheels moved beside them. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose too.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the living creatures rose from the earth, the wheels rose.

verses.rationale: Retains the unusual repeated spirit clause and shared animation.
verses.before: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, and the wheels rose along with them; for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
verses.after: Wherever the spirit would go, they went—that was where the spirit would go. The wheels rose alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
verses.tsw_comparator: Wherever the spirit was to go, they went, and the wheels rose along with them; for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full repeated explanation and all three paired motions.
verses.before: When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those rose from the earth, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
verses.after: When the creatures moved, the wheels moved; when they stood still, the wheels stood still. When the creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose alongside them, because the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
verses.tsw_comparator: When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those rose from the earth, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

verses.rationale: Keeps expanse and ice imagery with likeness qualification.
verses.before: Over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of an expanse, shining like awe-inspiring crystal, spread out above their heads.
verses.after: Above the heads of the living creatures was the likeness of an expanse, stretched out over them, gleaming like awe-inspiring ice.
verses.tsw_comparator: Over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of an expanse, shining like awe-inspiring crystal, spread out above their heads.

verses.rationale: Preserves the conspicuous duplication in the source rather than silently deleting it.
verses.before: And under the expanse their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another. And each creature had two wings covering its body on either side.
verses.after: Beneath the expanse their wings stretched straight toward one another. Each had two wings covering its body—two covering its body.
verses.tsw_comparator: And under the expanse their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another. And each creature had two wings covering its body on either side.

verses.rationale: Retains all three sound comparisons and the pause gesture.
verses.before: And when they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of many waters, like the sound of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let down their wings.
verses.after: As they moved, I heard the sound of their wings, like the roar of great waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a tumult like the noise of an army. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when they went, I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of many waters, like the sound of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the sound of an army. When they stood still, they let down their wings.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated lowering and the voice’s location.
verses.before: And there came a voice from above the expanse over their heads. When they stood still, they let down their wings.
verses.after: A voice came from above the expanse over their heads. When they stood still, they lowered their wings.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there came a voice from above the expanse over their heads. When they stood still, they let down their wings.

verses.rationale: Keeps the accumulating likeness qualifications before the human appearance.
verses.before: And above the expanse over their heads there was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like sapphire, and seated above the likeness of a throne was a likeness with a human appearance.
verses.after: Above the expanse over their heads was the likeness of a throne, with the appearance of sapphire. High above, on that throne-like form, was a likeness with a human appearance.
verses.tsw_comparator: And above the expanse over their heads there was the likeness of a throne, in appearance like sapphire, and seated above the likeness of a throne was a likeness with a human appearance.

verses.rationale: Retains waist boundary and difficult fire enclosure without over-specifying material.
verses.before: And upward from what had the appearance of his waist I saw, as it were, gleaming metal, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around. And downward from what had the appearance of his waist, I saw, as it were, the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.
verses.after: From what looked like his waist upward, I saw a gleam like glowing metal, like fire enclosed all around. From what looked like his waist downward, I saw something like fire, with brightness surrounding him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And upward from what had the appearance of his waist I saw, as it were, gleaming metal, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around. And downward from what had the appearance of his waist, I saw, as it were, the appearance of fire, and there was brightness around him.

verses.rationale: Keeps the final qualified identification and bodily response.
verses.before: Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. Such was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of one speaking.
verses.after: The brightness around him looked like the rainbow in a cloud on a rainy day. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell facedown and heard a voice speaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud on the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. Such was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of one speaking.

verses.rationale: Retains the recurring address and its contrast with the enthroned figure.
verses.before: And he said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
verses.after: He said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."

verses.rationale: Does not add an explicit divine title to the indefinite spirit.
verses.before: And a spirit entered into me as he spoke to me, and set me upon my feet, and I heard him speaking to me.
verses.after: As he spoke to me, a spirit entered me and set me on my feet. I heard him speaking to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: And a spirit entered into me as he spoke to me, and set me upon my feet, and I heard him speaking to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the unexpected plural nations and ongoing rebellion.
verses.before: And he said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against me; they and their fathers have transgressed against me to this very day.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against me. They and their ancestors have defied me to this very day.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the children of Israel, to a rebellious nation that has rebelled against me; they and their fathers have transgressed against me to this very day.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily imagery and introduces the recurring messenger formula.
verses.before: The children are obstinate and hard-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you will say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD.'
verses.after: Their children have hard faces and stubborn hearts. I am sending you to them, and you must tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’
verses.tsw_comparator: The children are obstinate and hard-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you shall say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD.'

verses.rationale: Maintains both possible responses and the recognition outcome.
verses.before: And whether they hear or refuse, for they are a rebellious house, they will know that a prophet has been among them.
verses.after: Whether they listen or refuse—for they are a rebellious household—they will know that a prophet has been among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And whether they hear or refuse, for they are a rebellious house, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated prohibitions and threatening plant/animal images.
verses.before: And you, son of man, do not fear them or their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be dismayed at their faces, for they are a rebellious house.
verses.after: And you, son of man, do not fear them or their words. Though briars and thorns surround you and you live among scorpions, do not fear their words or be dismayed by their faces. They are a rebellious household.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, son of man, do not fear them or their words, though briers and thorns are with you, and you dwell among scorpions. Do not fear their words or be dismayed at their faces, for they are a rebellious house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the mandate independent of the audience’s response.
verses.before: And you will speak my words to them, whether they hear or refuse, for they are rebellious.
verses.after: Speak my words to them whether they listen or refuse, for they are rebellious.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall speak my words to them, whether they hear or refuse, for they are rebellious.

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between prophet and audience and the concrete command.
verses.before: But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house; open your mouth and eat what I give you."
verses.after: But you, son of man, listen to what I am telling you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious household. Open your mouth and eat what I give you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But you, son of man, hear what I say to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house; open your mouth and eat what I give you."

verses.rationale: Renders the doubled attention marker as a single natural visual introduction.
verses.before: I looked, and look, a hand was extended to me, and there was a scroll of a book in it.
verses.after: I looked and saw a hand stretched out toward me, holding a scroll.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I looked, and behold, a hand was extended to me, and there was a scroll of a book in it.

verses.rationale: Keeps both written surfaces and the threefold contents.
verses.before: He spread it before me, and it was written on the front and on the back, and written on it were lamentations, mourning, and woe.
verses.after: He unrolled it before me. Writing covered its front and back: laments, mourning, and woe.
verses.tsw_comparator: He spread it before me, and it was written on the front and on the back, and written on it were lamentations, mourning, and woe.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated eating command and its sequence before speaking.
verses.before: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find; eat this scroll and go, speak to the house of Israel."
verses.after: He said to me, “Son of man, eat what is here. Eat this scroll, then go and speak to the house of Israel.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find; eat this scroll and go, speak to the house of Israel."

verses.rationale: Keeps divine agency in feeding rather than merely handing over.
verses.before: So I opened my mouth, and He gave me this scroll to eat.
verses.after: I opened my mouth, and he fed me the scroll.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I opened my mouth, and He gave me this scroll to eat.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily fullness and the surprising sweetness of a lament scroll.
verses.before: He said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I give you." So I ate it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll I am giving you.” I ate it, and in my mouth it was sweet as honey.
verses.tsw_comparator: And He said to me, "Son of man, feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I give you." So I ate it, and it was in my mouth as sweet as honey.

verses.rationale: Keeps words as the given content, not the prophet’s explanation.
verses.before: Then He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
verses.after: Then he said, “Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.

verses.rationale: Reorders the contrast to identify the destination first.
verses.before: For you are not sent to a people of unfamiliar speech and difficult tongue, but to the house of Israel,
verses.after: You are being sent to the house of Israel, not to a people whose speech is unfamiliar and whose language is hard to understand.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you are not sent to a people of unfamiliar speech and difficult tongue, but to the house of Israel,

verses.rationale: Keeps the counterfactual claim and repeated language difficulty.
verses.before: not to many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
verses.after: Nor are you being sent to many peoples with unfamiliar speech and difficult languages whose words you cannot understand. If I had sent you to them, they would have listened to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: not to many peoples of unfamiliar speech and difficult tongue, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.

verses.rationale: Preserves the causal link and paired head/heart descriptions.
verses.before: But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me. For all the house of Israel are hardened of forehead and stubborn of heart.
verses.after: But the house of Israel will refuse to listen to you, because they refuse to listen to me. The whole house of Israel is hardheaded and stubborn-hearted.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me. For all the house of Israel are hardened of forehead and stubborn of heart.

verses.rationale: Retains matching bodily images and divine preparation.
verses.before: Look, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.
verses.after: Look, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as theirs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.

verses.rationale: Keeps the hard mineral image and repeating reassurance.
verses.before: Like the hardest stone, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them, nor be dismayed at their faces, though they are a rebellious house."
verses.after: I have made your forehead like adamant, harder than flint. Do not fear them or be dismayed by their faces, for they are a rebellious household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Like the hardest stone, harder than flint, I have made your forehead. Do not fear them, nor be dismayed at their faces, though they are a rebellious house."

verses.rationale: Retains both heart and ears and all the words.
verses.before: He said to me, "Son of man, all my words that I will speak to you, receive in your heart and hear with your ears.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, take to heart every word I speak to you, and listen with your ears.
verses.tsw_comparator: And He said to me, "Son of man, all my words that I shall speak to you, receive in your heart and hear with your ears.

verses.rationale: Clarifies the exiles’ relationship to Ezekiel without adding nationality beyond context.
verses.before: And go, get you to the exiles, to your people, and speak to them. Say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD,' whether they hear or refuse."
verses.after: Go to the exiles, to your own people. Speak to them and tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says,’ whether they listen or refuse.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And go, get you to the exiles, to your people, and speak to them. Say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD,' whether they hear or refuse."

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned blessing wording rather than emending it to rising glory.
verses.before: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great earthquake: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from its place!"
verses.after: Then a spirit lifted me, and behind me I heard a great rumbling sound: “Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great earthquake: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from its place!"

verses.rationale: Keeps the three-part sound description and repeated rumble.
verses.before: It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and a sound of a great earthquake.
verses.after: I heard the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, the wheels beside them, and a great rumbling sound.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures touching one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, and a sound of a great earthquake.

verses.rationale: Preserves bitterness and heat without assigning a psychological cause.
verses.before: The Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness in the heat of my spirit, the hand of the LORD being strong upon me.
verses.after: The spirit lifted me and carried me away. I went in bitterness, my spirit burning, while the hand of the LORD rested heavily on me.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness in the heat of my spirit, the hand of the LORD being strong upon me.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form sat, preserving seven days and the repeated sitting.
verses.before: I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar Canal, and I sat where they were dwelling. And I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.
verses.after: I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived beside the Kebar River, and sat where they sat. For seven days I sat among them, stunned.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I came to the exiles at Tel Abib, who were dwelling by the Chebar Canal, and I sat where they were dwelling. And I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the interval and messenger transition.
verses.before: And at the end of seven days, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: At the end of seven days, the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: And at the end of seven days, the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Retains the watchman image and the warning’s source.
verses.before: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you will give them warning from me.
verses.after: “Son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, warn them for me.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you shall give them warning from me.

verses.rationale: Generic inclusive person preserves both individual guilt and prophetic blood-accountability.
verses.before: If I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that wicked person will die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at your hand.
verses.after: When I tell a wicked person, ‘You will certainly die,’ and you give no warning, saying nothing to warn that person away from a wicked path so they may live, that wicked person will die in their guilt. But I will hold you accountable for their blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I say to the wicked, 'You shall surely die,' and you give him no warning, nor speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life, that wicked person shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require at your hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps the person’s response distinct from the watchman’s responsibility.
verses.before: But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he will die in his iniquity, but you will have delivered your soul.
verses.after: If you warn a wicked person and they do not turn from their wickedness and their wicked path, they will die in their guilt, but you will have saved your own life.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he shall die in his iniquity, but you will have delivered your soul.

verses.rationale: Preserves the troubling divine stumbling block and all stated consequences.
verses.before: Again, if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he will die. Because you have not warned him, he will die for his sin, and his righteous deeds that he has done will not be remembered, but his blood I will require at your hand.
verses.after: Again, if a righteous person turns from doing right and does wrong, and I put a stumbling block before them, they will die. Because you did not warn them, they will die in their sin, and their righteous deeds will not be remembered. I will hold you accountable for their blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again, if a righteous person turns from his righteousness and commits injustice, and I lay a stumbling block before him, he shall die. Because you have not warned him, he shall die for his sin, and his righteous deeds that he has done shall not be remembered, but his blood I will require at your hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps warning, response, and both lives in the conditional sequence.
verses.before: But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live, because he took warning, and you will have delivered your soul."
verses.after: But if you warn a righteous person not to sin, and they do not sin, they will certainly live because they took warning, and you will have saved your own life.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, he shall surely live, because he took warning, and you will have delivered your soul."

verses.rationale: Retains hand and location as separate elements.
verses.before: And the hand of the LORD was upon me there, and He said to me, "Rise, go out into the valley, and there I will speak with you."
verses.after: There the hand of the LORD came upon me. He said, “Get up and go out to the valley. I will speak with you there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the hand of the LORD was upon me there, and He said to me, "Rise, go out into the valley, and there I will speak with you."

verses.rationale: Connects the new appearance explicitly to the earlier vision.
verses.before: So I rose and went out into the valley, and look, the glory of the LORD stood there, like the glory that I had seen by the Chebar Canal. And I fell on my face.
verses.after: I got up and went to the valley. There stood the glory of the LORD, like the glory I had seen beside the Kebar River. I fell facedown.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I rose and went out into the valley, and behold, the glory of the LORD stood there, like the glory that I had seen by the Chebar Canal. And I fell on my face.

verses.rationale: Keeps the spirit’s action and the command without inventing a new speaker.
verses.before: But the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself within your house.
verses.after: A spirit entered me and set me on my feet. He spoke to me: “Go and shut yourself inside your house.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the Spirit entered into me and set me on my feet, and He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself within your house.

verses.rationale: Leaves the binding agents unnamed as in the source.
verses.before: And you, son of man, look, cords will be placed upon you, and you will be bound with them, so that you cannot go out among the people.
verses.after: As for you, son of man, they will put ropes on you and bind you, so that you cannot go out among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, son of man, behold, cords will be placed upon you, and you shall be bound with them, so that you cannot go out among the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves physical silencing and its relation to rebuke.
verses.before: I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you will be mute and unable to be a reprover to them, for they are a rebellious house.
verses.after: I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth. You will be silent, unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious household.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will make your tongue cling to the roof of your mouth, so that you shall be mute and unable to be a reprover to them, for they are a rebellious house.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paired permissive forms and divine control of speech.
verses.before: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD.' He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house."
verses.after: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you will tell them, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says.’ Let whoever listens listen, and whoever refuses refuse, for they are a rebellious household.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you shall say to them, 'Thus says the LORD GOD.' He who hears, let him hear; and he who refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house."

verses.rationale: Retains the material and identifies the city at the end.
verses.before: And you, son of man, take for yourself a brick and set it before you and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem—
verses.after: “Now you, son of man, take a brick, set it before you, and inscribe a city on it—Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, son of man, take for yourself a brick and set it before you and engrave on it a city, Jerusalem—

verses.rationale: Keeps every component of the enacted siege.
verses.before: Set siege against it, build a siege wall against it, cast up a ramp against it, set camps against it, position battering rams all around it.
verses.after: Lay siege to it: build siegeworks against it, heap up a ramp, set up camps, and place battering rams around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Set siege against it, build a siege wall against it, cast up a ramp against it, set camps against it, position battering rams all around it.

verses.rationale: Retains doubled siege agency and identifies the act as a sign.
verses.before: And you, take an iron plate and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face against it; it will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This is a sign to the house of Israel.
verses.after: Take an iron griddle and set it as an iron wall between you and the city. Turn your face toward it: it will be under siege, and you will besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, take an iron plate and place it as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face against it; it shall be under siege, and you shall besiege it. This is a sign to the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily burden and guilt rather than only a time prediction.
verses.before: Lie on your left side and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it. According to the number of days that you lie on it, you will bear their iniquity.
verses.after: Then lie on your left side and put the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For as many days as you lie on that side, you will bear their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Lie on your left side and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it. According to the number of days that you lie on it, you shall bear their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Preserves the pinned 390 and years-to-days correspondence.
verses.before: For I assign to you the years of their iniquity, according to the number of days, three hundred and ninety days, and you will bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.
verses.after: I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days: 390 days. You will bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I assign to you the years of their iniquity, according to the number of days, three hundred and ninety days, and you shall bear the iniquity of the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Retains right-side read form and doubled day/year phrase.
verses.before: And when you have completed these, lie again on your right side. You will bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for forty days; a day for each year I assign to you.
verses.after: When you have finished those days, lie down again, this time on your right side. Bear the guilt of the house of Judah for forty days. I have assigned you a day for a year, a day for a year.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you have completed these, lie again on your right side. You shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for forty days; a day for each year I assign to you.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three enacted gestures.
verses.before: Direct your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and your arm will be bared, and you will prophesy against it.
verses.after: Turn your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, bare your arm, and prophesy against it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Direct your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and your arm shall be bared, and you shall prophesy against it.

verses.rationale: Preserves God as binding agent here without importing that agent into 3:25.
verses.before: Look, I will put cords on you so that you cannot turn from one side to another until you have completed the days of your siege.
verses.after: Look, I will put ropes on you so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I will put cords on you so that you cannot turn from one side to another until you have completed the days of your siege.

verses.rationale: Preserves six ingredients, one vessel, and repeated duration.
verses.before: Take for yourself wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and emmer, and put them in a single vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. You will eat it according to the number of the days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days.
verses.after: Take wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Put them in one vessel and make bread from them. Eat it throughout the 390 days you lie on your side.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take for yourself wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and emmer, and put them in a single vessel, and make bread of them for yourself. You shall eat it according to the number of the days that you lie on your side, three hundred and ninety days.

verses.rationale: Keeps the ancient weight and ration schedule.
verses.before: Your food that you eat will be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from time to time you will eat it.
verses.after: Weigh out your food: twenty shekels a day, eaten at set times.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your food that you eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day; from time to time you shall eat it.

verses.rationale: Retains ancient volume and parallel schedule.
verses.before: And water you will drink by measure, a sixth of a hin; from time to time you will drink.
verses.after: Measure your drinking water: one-sixth of a hin, drunk at set times.
verses.tsw_comparator: And water you shall drink by measure, a sixth of a hin; from time to time you shall drink.

verses.rationale: Makes dung the fuel rather than an ingredient.
verses.before: Eat it as a barley cake, baking it in their sight on human dung.
verses.after: Eat the bread as a barley cake, baking it over human dung in their sight.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Eat it as a barley cake, baking it in their sight on human dung.

verses.rationale: Keeps uncleanness and forced dispersal as the sign’s interpretation.
verses.before: Then the LORD said, "Thus will the people of Israel eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."
verses.after: The LORD said, “This is how the Israelites will eat their food unclean among the nations where I drive them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said, "Thus shall the people of Israel eat their bread unclean among the nations where I will drive them."

verses.rationale: Preserves the protest and distinct prohibited foods.
verses.before: Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Look, I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now, I have never eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has abominable flesh entered my mouth."
verses.after: I said, “Ah, Lord GOD! I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now I have never eaten an animal that died on its own or was torn by beasts. No tainted meat has entered my mouth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I have never defiled myself. From my youth until now, I have never eaten what died of itself or was torn by beasts, nor has abominable flesh entered my mouth."

verses.rationale: Renders the concession directly and keeps fuel relation clear.
verses.before: Then he said to me, "Look, I have given you cow dung instead of human dung, on which you may prepare your bread."
verses.after: He answered, “Then I will allow you cattle dung instead of human dung. Bake your bread over that.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, "Behold, I have given you cow dung instead of human dung, on which you may prepare your bread."

verses.rationale: Keeps staff-of-bread image alongside its rationing consequence.
verses.before: He also said to me, "Son of man, look, I will break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in dismay.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, I am about to break Jerusalem’s staff of bread. They will eat bread by weight in anxiety and drink water by measure in dismay.
verses.tsw_comparator: He also said to me, "Son of man, behold, I will break the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They shall eat bread by weight and in anxiety, and drink water by measure and in dismay.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual horror and guilt without reducing them to hunger alone.
verses.before: Because they lack bread and water, they will look at each other in dismay and waste away because of their iniquity."
verses.after: Food and water will run short. They will look at one another in horror and waste away in their guilt.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Because they lack bread and water, they will look at each other in dismay and waste away because of their iniquity."

verses.rationale: Keeps sword-as-razor, both shaved areas, and weighed division.
verses.before: And you, son of man, take for yourself a sharp sword, taking the barber's razor. Pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales for weighing and divide the hair.
verses.after: “And you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber’s razor. Pass it over your head and beard. Then take scales and divide the hair by weight.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you, son of man, take for yourself a sharp sword, taking the barber's razor. Pass it over your head and your beard. Then take scales for weighing and divide the hair.

verses.rationale: Preserves all thirds and the shift from symbolic hair to pursued people.
verses.before: A third you will burn with fire among the city, in the completion of the days of the siege. Then take a third and strike it with the sword all around her. A third you will scatter to the wind, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.
verses.after: When the days of the siege are complete, burn a third in the fire inside the city. Take another third and strike it with the sword around the city. Scatter the last third to the wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: A third you shall burn with fire in the midst of the city, in the completion of the days of the siege. Then take a third and strike it with the sword all around her. A third you shall scatter to the wind, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.

verses.rationale: Makes the referent of the few clear while keeping their location.
verses.before: And take from there a few in number and bind them in the folds of your garment.
verses.after: Take a few of those hairs and tie them in the folds of your garment.
verses.tsw_comparator: And take from there a few in number and bind them in the folds of your garment.

verses.rationale: Keeps loss even from preserved hairs and the fire’s wider reach.
verses.before: And of these again take some and throw them into the fire and burn them in the fire. From this fire will go out upon all the house of Israel.
verses.after: Then take some of these as well, throw them into the fire, and burn them. From it a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: And of these again take some and throw them into the fire and burn them in the fire. From this fire will go out upon all the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Keeps feminine city personification and central placement without geographic expansion.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: This is Jerusalem. I placed her among the nations, with countries all around her.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: This is Jerusalem. I set her among the nations, with other lands around her.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: This is Jerusalem. I placed her in the midst of the nations, with countries all around her.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift from personified city to its people and both legal terms.
verses.before: But she rebelled against my judgments with wickedness more than the nations and my statutes more than the lands all around her. They have rejected my judgments and have not walked in my statutes.
verses.after: Yet she rebelled against my judgments more wickedly than the nations, and against my statutes more than the lands around her. They rejected my judgments and did not live by my statutes.
verses.tsw_comparator: But she rebelled against my judgments with wickedness more than the nations and my statutes more than the lands all around her. They have rejected my judgments and have not walked in my statutes.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s final negative rather than harmonizing with 11:12.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations that are around you and have not walked in my statutes nor kept my judgments, nor have you done according to the judgments of the nations that are around you,
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: You have been more defiant than the nations around you. You have not lived by my statutes or carried out my judgments; you have not even followed the judgments of the nations around you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: Because you have been more turbulent than the nations that are around you and have not walked in my statutes nor kept my judgments, nor have you done according to the judgments of the nations that are around you,

verses.rationale: Clarifies the feminine addressee while retaining emphatic divine opposition.
verses.before: so, thus says the LORD GOD: Look, I am against you, even I, and will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.
verses.after: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: I myself am against you, Jerusalem. I will carry out judgments within you in the sight of the nations.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: Behold, I am against you, even I, and will execute judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.

verses.rationale: Retains the categorical claim without weakening it to unusual severity.
verses.before: I will do in you what I have not done, and the like of which I will not do again, because of all your abominations.
verses.after: Because of all your abominations, I will do among you what I have never done and will never do again.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will do in you what I have not done, and the like of which I will not do again, because of all your abominations.

verses.rationale: Names cannibalism plainly and preserves both familial directions.
verses.before: So fathers will eat their sons in your midst, and sons will eat their fathers. And I will execute judgments in you, and will scatter all your remnant to all the winds.
verses.after: So fathers among you will eat their children, and children will eat their fathers. I will carry out judgments against you and scatter all who remain of you to every wind.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore fathers shall eat their sons in your midst, and sons shall eat their fathers. And I will execute judgments in you, and will scatter all your remnant to all the winds.

verses.rationale: Retains oath, sanctuary defilement, and difficult cutting-down verb with note.
verses.before: So, as I live, declares the LORD GOD, surely because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I also will withdraw. My eye will not spare, and I also will not have pity.
verses.after: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and abominations, I too will cut you down. My eye will not spare you, and I will show no pity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD GOD, surely because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your detestable things and with all your abominations, I also will withdraw. My eye will not spare, and I also will not have pity.

verses.rationale: Retains all three outcomes and their correspondence with the hair sign.
verses.before: A third of you will die of pestilence and be consumed with famine in your midst, and a third will fall by the sword all around you, and a third I will scatter to all the winds, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.
verses.after: A third of you will die of plague and be consumed by famine within you. A third will fall by the sword around you. A third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
verses.tsw_comparator: A third of you shall die of pestilence and be consumed with famine in your midst, and a third shall fall by the sword all around you, and a third I will scatter to all the winds, and I will unsheathe the sword after them.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine satisfaction and jealousy without apologetic explanation.
verses.before: Thus will my anger be spent, and I will cause my wrath to rest upon them, and I will be comforted. Then they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal when I have spent my wrath upon them.
verses.after: Then my anger will be spent. I will let my fury rest upon them and be satisfied. When I have spent my fury on them, they will know that I, the LORD, spoke in my jealous zeal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus shall my anger be spent, and I will cause my wrath to rest upon them, and I will be comforted. Then they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my zeal when I have spent my wrath upon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the public audience and two outcomes.
verses.before: Moreover, I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of everyone who pass by.
verses.after: I will make you a ruin and an object of scorn among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone passing by.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, I will make you a desolation and a reproach among the nations that are around you, in the sight of all who pass by.

verses.rationale: Keeps the fourfold public effect and threefold wrath.
verses.before: So it will be a reproach, a taunt, a warning, and an astonishment to the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments in you in anger and in wrath and with furious rebukes. I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.after: You will become an object of scorn and taunting, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I carry out judgments against you in anger, fury, and furious rebukes. I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: So it will be a reproach, a taunt, a warning, and an astonishment to the nations that are around you, when I execute judgments in you in anger and in wrath and with furious rebukes. I, the LORD, have spoken.

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift them/you and both arrows and staff images.
verses.before: When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine, which will be for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, and I will increase the famine upon you and break your supply of bread.
verses.after: I will send deadly arrows of famine against them, arrows of destruction that I send to destroy you. I will increase the famine upon you and break your staff of bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine, which shall be for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, and I will increase the famine upon you and break your supply of bread.

verses.rationale: Retains bereavement and the full list of destructive agents.
verses.before: So I will send against you famine and wild beasts, and they will bereave you. Pestilence and blood will pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.after: I will send famine and wild beasts against you, and they will bereave you. Plague and bloodshed will pass through you, and I will bring a sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will send against you famine and wild beasts, and they will bereave you. Pestilence and blood shall pass through you, and I will bring the sword upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken.

verses.rationale: Retains the new oracle’s introduction.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps the mountains as addressed witnesses.
verses.before: "Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them,
verses.after: “Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them,

verses.rationale: Preserves both divine titles and all four landscape features.
verses.before: saying, 'Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD GOD: Thus says the LORD GOD to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and valleys: Look, I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.
verses.after: Say, ‘Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD! This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and hills, the ravines and valleys: I myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
verses.tsw_comparator: saying, 'Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the LORD GOD: Thus says the LORD GOD to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and valleys: Behold, I am bringing a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places.

verses.rationale: Retains the distinct cultic objects and bodily placement.
verses.before: Your altars will be desolate, your incense altars shattered, and I will cast down your slain before your idols.
verses.after: Your altars will be devastated and your incense altars broken. I will throw your slain down before your idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your altars shall be desolate, your incense altars shattered, and I will cast down your slain before your idols.

verses.rationale: Keeps the change from their to your as accusation intensifies.
verses.before: I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and scatter your bones around your altars.
verses.after: I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols and scatter your bones around your altars.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will lay the corpses of the Israelites before their idols, and scatter your bones around your altars.

verses.rationale: Preserves each object and the cumulative destruction rather than compressing the list.
verses.before: In all your dwellings the cities will be laid waste, and the high places will be desolate, so that your altars may be destroyed and be made desolate, your idols may be broken and come to an end, your incense altars may be cut down, and your works may be blotted out.
verses.after: Wherever you live, the towns will be ruined and the high places devastated. Your altars will lie ruined and desolate, your idols shattered and gone, your incense altars cut down, and your handiwork wiped out.
verses.tsw_comparator: In all your dwellings the cities shall be laid waste, and the high places shall be desolate, so that your altars may be destroyed and be made desolate, your idols may be broken and come to an end, your incense altars may be cut down, and your works may be blotted out.

verses.rationale: Keeps the recognition formula intact.
verses.before: The slain will fall in your midst, and you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.after: The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that I am the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps survivors within the dispersion rather than promising immediate return.
verses.before: Yet I will leave a remnant, when you have some who escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the countries.
verses.after: “‘Yet I will leave some alive. Some of you will escape the sword among the nations when you are scattered through other lands.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will leave a remnant, when you have some who escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered among the countries.

verses.rationale: Retains the passive I was broken and sexual metaphor with a note on difficult syntax.
verses.before: Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their adulterous heart that has turned away from me, and with their eyes that have turned after their idols. And they will loathe themselves for the evils which they committed in all their abominations.
verses.after: Then your survivors will remember me among the nations where they have been taken captive—how I was broken by their unfaithful heart that turned away from me, and by their eyes that went whoring after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evil they did, for all their abominations.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive, how I have been broken with their adulterous heart that has turned away from me, and with their eyes that have turned after their idols. And they will loathe themselves for the evils which they committed in all their abominations.

verses.rationale: Makes the final clause’s relation to the announced disaster clear.
verses.before: And they will know that I am the LORD; I did not speak in vain concerning bringing this evil upon them.
verses.after: They will know that I am the LORD, that I did not speak idly when I said I would bring this disaster on them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And they shall know that I am the LORD; I did not speak in vain concerning bringing this evil upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the prophet’s gestures, cry, and three threats.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: Clap your hands, stamp your feet, and say, 'Alas,' because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel. By the sword, by famine, and by pestilence they will fall.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: Strike your hands together, stamp your foot, and cry, ‘Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel!’ They will fall by sword, famine, and plague.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: Clap your hands, stamp your feet, and say, 'Alas,' because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel. By the sword, by famine, and by pestilence they shall fall.

verses.rationale: Retains three locations and their distinct fates.
verses.before: He who is far off will die of pestilence; he who is near will fall by the sword; he who remains and is besieged will die by famine. Thus will I spend my fury upon them.
verses.after: Those far away will die of plague; those nearby will fall by the sword. Those who remain, shut inside, will die of famine. I will spend my fury on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: He who is far off shall die of pestilence; he who is near shall fall by the sword; he who remains and is besieged shall die by famine. Thus will I spend my fury upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete landscape catalogue and sacrificial aroma language.
verses.before: And you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain are among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak, the places where they offered pleasing aromas to all their idols.
verses.after: You will know that I am the LORD when their slain lie among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill and every mountaintop, beneath every green tree and every leafy oak—wherever they offered a pleasing aroma to all their idols.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you shall know that I am the LORD, when their slain are among their idols, around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak, the places where they offered pleasing aromas to all their idols.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Diblah rather than silently replacing it with Riblah.
verses.before: I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness of Diblah wherever they dwell. Then they will know that I am the LORD.'"
verses.after: I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land desolate and waste, from the wilderness of Diblah wherever they dwell. Then they shall know that I am the LORD.'"

verses.rationale: Marks the next oracle.
verses.before: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: The word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps repetition and fourfold extent in prophetic lineation.
verses.before: "As for you, son of man, thus says the LORD GOD to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.
verses.after: “And you, son of man—this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come to the four corners of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: "As for you, son of man, thus says the LORD GOD to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four corners of the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves three first-person judgment actions.
verses.before: Now the end is upon you, and I will send my anger on you. I will judge you according to your ways, and I will place all your abominations against you.
verses.after: Now the end is upon you. I will unleash my anger against you, judge you by your ways, and bring all your abominations back upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the end is upon you, and I will send my anger on you. I will judge you according to your ways, and I will place all your abominations against you.

verses.rationale: Keeps abominations remaining rather than reducing them to punishment alone.
verses.before: My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity. I will repay your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
verses.after: My eye will not spare you; I will show no pity. I will bring your ways back upon you, and your abominations will remain among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity. I will repay your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD."

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned one disaster phrase with uncertainty in the note.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: A disaster, a unique disaster, look, it is coming!
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: Disaster—a singular disaster! Look, it is coming.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: A disaster, a unique disaster, behold, it is coming!

verses.rationale: Retains end/awakened imagery and repetition.
verses.before: An end has come; the end has come; it has awakened against you. Look, it is coming!
verses.after: An end has come; the end has come! It has awakened against you. Look, it is coming.
verses.tsw_comparator: An end has come; the end has come; it has awakened against you. Behold, it is coming!

verses.rationale: Keeps doom and contrast while noting uncertain rare words.
verses.before: Doom has come upon you, dweller in the land. The time has come; the day is near. There is tumult and not joyful shouting on the mountains.
verses.after: Doom has come to you who live in the land. The time has come; the day is near— tumult, not joyful shouts on the mountains.
verses.tsw_comparator: Doom has come upon you, dweller in the land. The time has come; the day is near. There is tumult and not joyful shouting on the mountains.

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel wrath and judicial clauses.
verses.before: Now I will shortly pour out my wrath upon you and spend my anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways, and I will repay you for all your abominations.
verses.after: Very soon I will pour out my fury on you and spend my anger against you. I will judge you by your ways and bring all your abominations back upon you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I will shortly pour out my wrath upon you and spend my anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways, and I will repay you for all your abominations.

verses.rationale: Retains the expanded recognition formula who strikes.
verses.before: My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity. I will make your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I, the LORD, strike.
verses.after: My eye will not spare; I will show no pity. I will repay you according to your ways, and your abominations will remain among you. Then you will know that I am the LORD who strikes.
verses.tsw_comparator: My eye will not spare you, nor will I have pity. I will make your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst. Then you will know that I, the LORD, strike.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired botanical images and urgent repeated look.
verses.before: Look, the day! Look, it comes! Doom has gone forth. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.
verses.after: Look—the day! Look, it comes! Doom has gone out. The rod has budded; arrogance has blossomed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, the day! Behold, it comes! Doom has gone forth. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.

verses.rationale: Preserves the four negatives while marking difficult final nouns for review.
verses.before: Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them will remain, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nor anything eminent among them.
verses.after: Violence has risen into a rod of wickedness. None of them will remain, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nothing of distinction among them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. None of them shall remain, none of their multitude, none of their wealth, nor anything eminent among them.

verses.rationale: Keeps both commercial responses and comprehensive wrath.
verses.before: The time has come; the day has drawn near. Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is against all their multitude.
verses.after: The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice or the seller mourn, for wrath is upon the whole multitude.
verses.tsw_comparator: The time has come; the day has drawn near. Let not the buyer rejoice, nor the seller mourn, for wrath is against all their multitude.

verses.rationale: Retains return language and difficult life/guilt clause without inserting a jubilee date.
verses.before: For the seller will not return to what he has sold while they live, for the vision is against all their multitude. It will not turn back, and no one will preserve their life in their iniquity.
verses.after: The seller will not return to what was sold, even if both remain alive. The vision against the whole multitude will not be reversed. No one will hold on to life through their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the seller shall not return to what he has sold while they live, for the vision is against all their multitude. It shall not turn back, and no one shall preserve their life in their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps preparation’s failure and its stated cause.
verses.before: They have blown the trumpet and prepared everything, but none goes to battle, for my wrath is against all their multitude.
verses.after: They have sounded the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes to battle, for my wrath is upon the whole multitude.
verses.tsw_comparator: They have blown the trumpet and prepared everything, but none goes to battle, for my wrath is against all their multitude.

verses.rationale: Preserves spatial contrast and devouring image.
verses.before: The sword is outside, and the plague and famine are inside. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city, famine and plague will consume them.
verses.after: Outside is the sword; inside are plague and famine. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword; whoever is in the city, famine and plague will devour.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sword is outside, and the plague and famine are inside. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city, famine and plague will consume them.

verses.rationale: Retains doves and individual guilt in collective flight.
verses.before: But people who escape of them will escape and be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his iniquity.
verses.after: Those who escape will flee to the mountains, like doves from the valleys, all of them moaning, each over their own guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: But those who escape of them shall escape and be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his iniquity.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s bodily image; note allows weakness or loss of bladder control.
verses.before: All hands will be feeble, and all knees will flow with water.
verses.after: Every hand will hang limp, and every knee will run with water.
verses.tsw_comparator: All hands will be feeble, and all knees will flow with water.

verses.rationale: Preserves four bodily signs of fear and mourning.
verses.before: They will wear sackcloth, and trembling will cover them. Shame will be on all their faces, and baldness on all their heads.
verses.after: They will put on sackcloth, and trembling will cover them. Every face will be ashamed, every head shaved bare.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will wear sackcloth, and trembling will cover them. Shame will be on all their faces, and baldness on all their heads.

verses.rationale: Keeps wealth’s ritual, protective, and nutritional failures.
verses.before: They will cast their silver in the streets, and their gold will be like an unclean thing. Their silver and gold will not be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath. They will not satisfy their souls, nor fill their stomachs, for it has become a stumbling block of their iniquity.
verses.after: They will throw their silver into the streets and treat their gold as something unclean. Their silver and gold cannot rescue them on the day of the LORD’s fury. It cannot satisfy their appetite or fill their stomachs, for it became the stumbling block of their guilt.
verses.tsw_comparator: They shall cast their silver in the streets, and their gold will be like an unclean thing. Their silver and gold will not be able to deliver them in the day of the LORD’s wrath. They will not satisfy their souls, nor fill their stomachs, for it has become a stumbling block of their iniquity.

verses.rationale: Uses ornaments reading while noting possible sanctuary referent.
verses.before: As for the beauty of their ornaments, they set it for pride, and they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things in it. Therefore, I have made it an unclean thing to them.
verses.after: They made their beautiful ornaments a source of pride and fashioned from them their abominable images, their detestable things. So I have made that treasure unclean to them.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for the beauty of their ornaments, they set it for pride, and they made the images of their abominations and their detestable things in it. Therefore, I have made it an unclean thing to them.

verses.rationale: Follows the read form they will profane it and preserves both recipients.
verses.before: I will give it into the hands of foreigners as spoil and to the wicked of the earth as plunder, and they will profane it.
verses.after: I will hand it over to foreigners as plunder, to the wicked of the earth as loot, and they will profane it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give it into the hands of foreigners as spoil and to the wicked of the earth as plunder, and they will profane it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concealed/treasured place without defining its architecture.
verses.before: I will turn my face from them, and they will profane my treasured place. Robbers will come into it and profane it.
verses.after: I will turn my face away from them. They will profane my treasured place; violent men will enter it and profane it.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will turn my face from them, and they will profane my treasured place. Robbers will come into it and profane it.

verses.rationale: Preserves chain command and judicial bloodshed.
verses.before: "Forge a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes and the city is full of violence.
verses.after: “Make the chain! The land is full of bloodstained judgments, and the city is full of violence.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Forge a chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes and the city is full of violence.

verses.rationale: Keeps the superlative invaders and loss of houses and holy places.
verses.before: So I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will possess their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned.
verses.after: I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses. I will end the pride of the strong, and their sanctuaries will be profaned.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I will bring the worst of the nations, and they shall possess their houses. I will end the pride of the mighty, and their holy places will be profaned.

verses.rationale: Retains futile search with clipped cadence.
verses.before: Anguish comes, and they will seek peace, but there will be none.
verses.after: Anguish is coming. They will look for peace, but there will be none.
verses.tsw_comparator: Anguish comes, and they will seek peace, but there will be none.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated news and three failed sources of guidance.
verses.before: Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor will be upon rumor. They will seek a vision from the prophet, but the law will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.
verses.after: Disaster will follow disaster, report will follow report. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction will vanish from the priest and counsel from the elders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Disaster upon disaster will come, and rumor shall be upon rumor. They will seek a vision from the prophet, but the law will perish from the priest and counsel from the elders.

verses.rationale: Keeps three social groups and judgment according to their own standards.
verses.before: The king will mourn, and the prince will be clothed with desolation. The hands of the people of the land will tremble. According to their way, I will deal with them, and by their judgments, I will judge them. Then they will know that I am the LORD."
