verses.after: The king will mourn, the prince will put on desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will shake. I will deal with them according to their ways and judge them by their own judgments. Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king will mourn, and the prince will be clothed with desolation. The hands of the people of the land will tremble. According to their way, I will deal with them, and by their judgments, I will judge them. Then they shall know that I am the LORD."

verses.rationale: Preserves precise date and the vision’s seated setting.
verses.before: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, with the elders of Judah sitting before me, the hand of the LORD GOD fell upon me there.
verses.after: In the sixth year, on the fifth day of the sixth month, I was sitting in my house with the elders of Judah seated before me. There the hand of the Lord GOD fell upon me.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I sat in my house, with the elders of Judah sitting before me, the hand of the LORD GOD fell upon me there.

verses.rationale: Retains pinned fire rather than silently reading man.
verses.before: I looked, and look, a form that appeared as fire. From what seemed the appearance of his waist downward was fire, and from his waist upward, the appearance of a bright glow, like glowing metal.
verses.after: I looked and saw a likeness with the appearance of fire. From what looked like his waist downward was fire; from his waist upward was a radiant gleam like glowing metal.
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked, and behold, a form that appeared as fire. From what seemed the appearance of his waist downward was fire, and from his waist upward, the appearance of a bright glow, like glowing metal.

verses.rationale: Keeps visionary mode, bodily action, direction, and doubled jealousy.
verses.before: He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by the lock of my head, and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.
verses.after: He stretched out what looked like a hand and took me by a lock of hair. A spirit lifted me between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate facing north. There stood the image of jealousy that provokes jealousy.
verses.tsw_comparator: He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by the lock of my head, and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where was the seat of the image of jealousy, which provokes to jealousy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the explicit connection to the previous manifestation.
verses.before: And look, the glory of the God of Israel was there, like the vision that I saw in the valley.
verses.after: There was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision I had seen in the valley.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, the glory of the God of Israel was there, like the vision that I saw in the valley.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated direction and exact gate relation.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Son of man, lift up your eyes now toward the north.” So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and look, north of the altar gate was this image of jealousy at the entrance.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, look toward the north.” I looked north, and there, north of the altar gate at the entrance, was that image of jealousy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Son of man, lift up your eyes now toward the north.” So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and behold, north of the altar gate was this image of jealousy at the entrance.

verses.rationale: Makes the implied divine departure explicit while noting its ambiguous subject.
verses.before: And he said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing? The great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? But you will see still greater abominations.”
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing? The great abominations the house of Israel commits here drive me far from my sanctuary. But you will see still greater abominations.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they are doing? The great abominations that the house of Israel is committing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? But you will see still greater abominations.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the sequence of arrival and discovery.
verses.before: Then he brought me to the door of the court, and I looked, and look, a hole in the wall.
verses.after: He brought me to the entrance of the court. I looked and saw a hole in the wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought me to the door of the court, and I looked, and behold, a hole in the wall.

verses.rationale: Preserves command and enacted response.
verses.before: He said to me, “Son of man, dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall, and look, an entrance.
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, dig through the wall.” I dug through it and found a doorway.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to me, “Son of man, dig through the wall.” So I dug through the wall, and behold, an entrance.

verses.rationale: Retains moral descriptor without adding explanation.
verses.before: And he said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are doing here.”
verses.after: He said, “Go in and see the evil abominations they are committing here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “Go in and see the wicked abominations they are doing here.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the complete depicted categories and encircling walls.
verses.before: So I went in and saw, and look, all kinds of forms of creeping things, abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, carved on the wall around.
verses.after: I went in and looked. All around the walls were engraved every kind of creeping creature and detestable animal, and all the idols of the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I went in and saw, and behold, all kinds of forms of creeping things, abominable animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel, carved on the wall around.

verses.rationale: Retains number, named elder, individual censers, and thick cloud.
verses.before: Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had his censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense went up.
verses.after: Seventy men from the elders of the house of Israel stood before them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan among them. Each held a censer, and a thick cloud of incense rose.
verses.tsw_comparator: Seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel were standing before them, with Jaazaniah the son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had his censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense went up.

verses.rationale: Keeps both quoted claims and private image chambers.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, each in his room of pictures? For they say, ‘The Lord does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’”
verses.after: He said, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, each in his chamber of images? They say, ‘The LORD does not see us. The LORD has abandoned the land.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel do in the dark, each in his room of pictures? For they say, ‘The Lord does not see us; the LORD has forsaken the land.’”

verses.rationale: Retains the escalating refrain.
verses.before: He also said to me, “You will see still greater abominations that they commit.”
verses.after: He said, “You will see still greater abominations that they are committing.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He also said to me, “You will see still greater abominations that they commit.”

verses.rationale: Names the deity without inserting a ritual reconstruction.
verses.before: Then he brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and look, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.
verses.after: He brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the LORD’s house. There women sat weeping for Tammuz.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and behold, there sat women weeping for Tammuz.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated question and escalation.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater abominations than these.”
verses.after: He said, “Have you seen this, son of man? You will see abominations even greater than these.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater abominations than these.”

verses.rationale: Keeps approximate count, three temple references, and bodily orientation.
verses.before: And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD. And look, at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, worshiping the sun toward the east.
verses.after: He brought me into the inner court of the LORD’s house. At the entrance to the LORD’s temple, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men. Their backs were toward the LORD’s temple and their faces eastward; they were bowing eastward to the sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD. And behold, at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, worshiping the sun toward the east.

verses.rationale: Retains the obscure gesture literally and connects cultic acts with violence.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations that they commit here, that they should also fill the land with violence and provoke me further to anger? And look, they are sending the branch to their nose.
verses.after: He said, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is it a small thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations they have committed here? They have filled the land with violence and keep provoking me. Look at them putting the branch to their noses!
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “Have you seen this, son of man? Is it too light a thing for the house of Judah to commit the abominations that they commit here, that they should also fill the land with violence and provoke me further to anger? And behold, they are sending the branch to their nose.

verses.rationale: Keeps the loud appeal and explicit refusal.
verses.before: So I will also act in fury. My eye will not spare, nor will I have pity. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them.”
verses.after: So I too will act in fury. My eye will not spare, and I will show no pity. Even if they shout loudly in my ears, I will not listen to them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I will also act in fury. My eye will not spare, nor will I have pity. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not hear them.”

verses.rationale: Preserves ambiguity of appointed agents without naming angels.
verses.before: Then he called out in my hearing with a loud voice, saying, "Let people who have charge over the city draw near, each with his destructive weapon in his hand."
verses.after: Then he called out loudly within my hearing: “Bring near those appointed over the city, each with a weapon of destruction in his hand!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he called out in my hearing with a loud voice, saying, "Let those who have charge over the city draw near, each with his destructive weapon in his hand."

verses.rationale: Retains six men and separately described linen figure without forcing total count.
verses.before: And look, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand. One man among them was clothed in linen, with a writing case at his waist. They went in and stood beside the bronze altar.
verses.after: Six men came from the direction of the upper gate facing north, each carrying a smashing weapon. Among them was a man dressed in linen, with a scribe’s writing kit at his waist. They came and stood beside the bronze altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand. One man among them was clothed in linen, with a writing case at his waist. They went in and stood beside the bronze altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement of glory and singular cherub.
verses.before: Now the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the cherub on which it rested to the threshold of the house. He called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writing case at his waist,
verses.after: The glory of the God of Israel rose from above the cherub where it had rested and moved to the threshold of the house. He called to the man dressed in linen with the writing kit at his waist.

verses.before: People give gifts to every prostitute, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from every side for your prostitutions.
verses.after: People give gifts to prostitutes, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from all around for your prostitution.
verses.tsw_comparator: People give gifts to every prostitute, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers. You bribed them to come to you from every side for your prostitutions.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated reversal rather than compressing it.
verses.before: You were the opposite of other women in your prostitutions: no one pursued you. You gave payment, but no payment was given to you. You became the opposite.
verses.after: Your prostitution was the opposite of other women’s. No one sought you out as a prostitute. You paid a fee, and no fee was paid to you. You were the opposite!
verses.tsw_comparator: You were the opposite of other women in your prostitutions: no one pursued you. You gave payment, but no payment was given to you. You became the opposite.

verses.rationale: Retains the direct denunciatory address to the city.
verses.before: So, prostitute, hear the word of the LORD.
verses.after: “‘Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, prostitute, hear the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps difficult poured-out noun as lust with literal copper alternative in note.
verses.before: This is what the LORD GOD says: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness exposed through your prostitutions with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them,
verses.after: This is what the Lord GOD says: Because you poured out your lust and exposed your nakedness in prostitution with your lovers and all your abominable idols, and because of the blood of your children whom you gave to them,
verses.tsw_comparator: This is what the LORD GOD says: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness exposed through your prostitutions with your lovers and with all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children that you gave to them,

verses.rationale: Preserves divine agency and forced exposure without softening the harm.
verses.before: so, I will gather all your lovers, those with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side, expose your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.
verses.after: I will gather all your lovers with whom you took pleasure, everyone you loved and everyone you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and expose your nakedness to them. They will see all your nakedness.
verses.tsw_comparator: therefore, I will gather all your lovers, those with whom you found pleasure, all those you loved and all those you hated. I will gather them against you from every side, expose your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.

verses.rationale: Keeps both charges and jealousy without moralizing beyond the speech.
verses.before: I will judge you with the judgments given to adulteresses and people who shed blood. I will make you blood in wrath and jealousy.
verses.after: I will judge you as adulterous women and women who shed blood are judged. I will bring upon you the bloodshed of fury and jealousy.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will judge you with the judgments given to adulteresses and those who shed blood. I will make you blood in wrath and jealousy.

verses.rationale: Retains every action in the stripping and destruction sequence.
verses.before: I will give you into their hand. They will tear down your mound and demolish your high places. They will strip you of your garments, take your beautiful ornaments, and leave you naked and bare.
verses.after: I will hand you over to them. They will demolish your mound, tear down your raised platforms, strip off your clothes, take your splendid ornaments, and leave you naked and bare.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will give you into their hand. They will tear down your mound and demolish your high places. They will strip you of your garments, take your beautiful ornaments, and leave you naked and bare.

verses.rationale: Names collective violence and dismembering explicitly.
verses.before: They will bring up an assembly against you, stone you with stones, and cut you to pieces with their swords.
verses.after: They will bring a mob against you, stone you, and cut you to pieces with their swords.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will bring up an assembly against you, stone you with stones, and cut you to pieces with their swords.

verses.rationale: Keeps houses and women witnesses within city allegory.
verses.before: They will burn your houses with fire and execute judgments against you before the eyes of many women. I will stop you from being a prostitute, and you will give payment no more.
verses.after: They will burn your houses and carry out judgments against you before many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will no longer pay fees.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will burn your houses with fire and execute judgments against you before the eyes of many women. I will stop you from being a prostitute, and you will give payment no more.

verses.rationale: Preserves anger’s cessation as spoken claim, not explanatory endorsement.
verses.before: Then I will let my wrath rest on you, and my jealousy will turn away from you. I will be quiet and no longer be angry.
verses.after: Then I will let my fury rest upon you, and my jealousy will leave you. I will be quiet and no longer angry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I will let my wrath rest on you, and my jealousy will turn away from you. I will be quiet and no longer be angry.

verses.rationale: Follows second-person read forms; renders final negative as rhetorical question with alternative noted.
verses.before: Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged me with all these things, therefore I too will bring your way down upon your head, declares the LORD GOD. Have you not added lewdness to all your abominations?
verses.after: Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged me with all these things, I in turn will bring your ways down on your head, declares the Lord GOD. Have you not added lewdness to all your abominations?
verses.tsw_comparator: Because you did not remember the days of your youth but enraged me with all these things, therefore I too will bring your way down upon your head, declares the LORD GOD. Have you not added lewdness to all your abominations?

verses.rationale: Keeps the compact proverb without rewording merely for difference.
verses.before: Look, everyone who uses proverbs about you will use this proverb: “Like mother, like daughter.”
verses.after: “‘Everyone who uses proverbs will use this one about you: “Like mother, like daughter.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, everyone who uses proverbs about you will use this proverb: “Like mother, like daughter.”

verses.rationale: Keeps parallel kinship insults and repeated parentage.
verses.before: You are the daughter of your mother, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.
verses.after: You are your mother’s daughter: she loathed her husband and children. You are your sisters’ sister: they loathed their husbands and children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are the daughter of your mother, who loathed her husband and her children; and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite, and your father an Amorite.

verses.rationale: Keeps kinship and left/right orientation; note explains north/south frame.
verses.before: Your older sister is Samaria, who lives to your north with her daughters; and your younger sister is Sodom, who lives to your south with her daughters.
verses.after: Your older sister is Samaria, who lives to your left with her daughters. Your younger sister, who lives to your right, is Sodom with her daughters.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your older sister is Samaria, who lives to your north with her daughters; and your younger sister is Sodom, who lives to your south with her daughters.

verses.rationale: Renders compressed little phrase as intensification with note.
verses.before: Yet you did not merely walk in their ways and do their abominations. In a very little while, you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.
verses.after: You did not merely follow their ways or practice their abominations. As though that were too little, you became more corrupt than they were in all your ways.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you did not merely walk in their ways and do their abominations. In a very little while, you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.

verses.rationale: Preserves oath and comparative accusation.
verses.before: As I live, declares the LORD GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done.
verses.after: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did what you and your daughters have done.
verses.tsw_comparator: As I live, declares the LORD GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters have not done as you and your daughters have done.

verses.rationale: Keeps complete stated sins and hand image without substituting later debates.
verses.before: Look, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, abundance of food, and careless ease belonged to her and her daughters; yet she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
verses.after: This was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, plenty of food, and untroubled ease, but they did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, this was the iniquity of your sister Sodom: pride, abundance of food, and careless ease belonged to her and her daughters; yet she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.

verses.rationale: Retains undefined abomination and source’s seeing clause.
verses.before: They became haughty and committed abomination before me. So I removed them when I saw it.
verses.after: They grew haughty and committed an abomination before me, so I removed them when I saw it.
verses.tsw_comparator: They became haughty and committed abomination before me. So I removed them when I saw it.

verses.rationale: Keeps quantitative comparison and relative righteousness.
verses.before: Samaria did not sin half as much as you. You multiplied your abominations beyond theirs and made your sisters appear righteous by all the abominations you committed.
verses.after: Samaria did not commit half your sins. You multiplied your abominations beyond theirs and made your sisters appear righteous by all the abominations you committed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Samaria did not sin half as much as you. You multiplied your abominations beyond theirs and made your sisters appear righteous by all the abominations you committed.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated disgrace and comparison rather than declaring sisters guiltless.
verses.before: You also, bear your disgrace—you who argued for your sisters. Because of your sins, in which you acted more abominably than they, they appear more righteous than you. Be ashamed, then, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters appear righteous.
verses.after: Bear your disgrace, you who have passed judgment on your sisters. Your sins are more abominable than theirs, so they appear more righteous than you. Be ashamed and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters appear righteous.
verses.tsw_comparator: You also, bear your disgrace—you who argued for your sisters. Because of your sins, in which you acted more abominably than they, they appear more righteous than you. Be ashamed, then, and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters appear righteous.

verses.rationale: Keeps all recipients of restoration and repeated fortunes.
verses.before: I will restore their fortunes: the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and your fortunes with theirs,
verses.after: “‘I will restore their fortunes—the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters—and restore your fortunes among them,
verses.tsw_comparator: I will restore their fortunes: the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters, the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and your fortunes with theirs,

verses.rationale: Keeps consolation’s uncomfortable relationship to Jerusalem’s disgrace.
verses.before: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, when you become a comfort to them.
verses.after: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all you have done, bringing them consolation.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, when you become a comfort to them.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three parallel returns.
verses.before: Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state; Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state; and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
verses.after: Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state; Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state; and you and your daughters will return to yours.
verses.tsw_comparator: Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state; Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state; and you and your daughters will return to your former state.

verses.rationale: Keeps former silence and continuing sentence.
verses.before: Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,
verses.after: You would not even mention your sister Sodom in the days of your pride,
verses.tsw_comparator: Was not your sister Sodom a byword in your mouth in the day of your pride,

verses.rationale: Retains pinned Aram and personified daughters rather than switching to Edom.
verses.before: before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you are scorned by the daughters of Aram and all around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines, people who despise you on every side.
verses.after: before your own wickedness was exposed. Now you are scorned by the daughters of Aram and all her neighbors, the daughters of the Philistines, who despise you on every side.
verses.tsw_comparator: before your wickedness was uncovered? Now you are scorned by the daughters of Aram and all around her, and by the daughters of the Philistines, those who despise you on every side.

verses.rationale: Keeps responsibility statement and shorter divine title.
verses.before: You yourself bear your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
verses.after: You must bear your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: You yourself bear your lewdness and your abominations, declares the LORD.

verses.rationale: Follows read form I will do and preserves oath/covenant distinction.
verses.before: For this is what the LORD GOD says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath in breaking the covenant.
verses.after: “‘For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you as you have dealt, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this is what the LORD GOD says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath in breaking the covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine remembering in contrast to city’s forgetting.
verses.before: Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.
verses.after: Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth and establish an everlasting covenant with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish for you an everlasting covenant.

verses.rationale: Retains changed kinship and difficult covenant qualification without resolving it.
verses.before: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both those older than you and those younger than you. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your covenant.
verses.after: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both older and younger. I will give them to you as daughters, though not on the basis of your covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, both those older than you and those younger than you. I will give them to you as daughters, but not because of your covenant.

verses.rationale: Keeps emphatic divine agency and continued purpose clause.
verses.before: I myself will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,
verses.after: I myself will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: I myself will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,

verses.rationale: Retains atonement and silencing rather than reducing ending to simple reassurance.
verses.before: so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the LORD GOD.’”
verses.after: so that you may remember and be ashamed, unable to open your mouth again because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for everything you have done, declares the Lord GOD.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you may remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the LORD GOD.’”

verses.rationale: Introduces the riddle oracle.
verses.before: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps both literary forms.
verses.before: "Son of man, pose a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel.
verses.after: “Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Son of man, pose a riddle, and speak a parable to the house of Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the bird’s full description and tree setting in lineated riddle.
verses.before: Say, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: A great eagle, great of wings, with long feathers, full of multi-colored plumage, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
verses.after: Say, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says: A great eagle, great of wing, with long feathers and thick, colorful plumage, came to Lebanon and took the top of a cedar.
verses.tsw_comparator: Say, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: A great eagle, great of wings, with long feathers, full of multi-colored plumage, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired commercial locations and highest shoot.
verses.before: He plucked off the topmost of its young twigs and brought it to the land of merchants; he set it in a city of traders.
verses.after: He plucked the highest of its young shoots, carried it to a land of merchants, and set it in a city of traders.
verses.tsw_comparator: He plucked off the topmost of its young twigs and brought it to the land of merchants; he set it in a city of traders.

verses.rationale: Preserves seed-to-vine development and willow comparison.
verses.before: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in a fertile field; he planted it beside abundant waters, like a willow tree.
verses.after: He took seed from the land and set it in a field for sowing. He placed it beside abundant water, setting it like a willow.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took some of the seed of the land and planted it in a fertile field; he planted it beside abundant waters, like a willow tree.

verses.rationale: Keeps spatial dependence and repeated vine development.
verses.before: It sprouted and became a spreading vine of low height, its branches turned toward him; and its roots were under it. So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.
verses.after: It sprouted and became a low, spreading vine, its branches turned toward him, its roots beneath him. It became a vine, put out branches, and sent out shoots.
verses.tsw_comparator: It sprouted and became a spreading vine of low height, its branches turned toward him; and its roots were under it. So it became a vine, produced branches, and sent out shoots.

verses.rationale: Preserves change of eagle and seeking water despite prior abundance.
verses.before: But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers, and look, this vine bent its roots toward him, and sent out its branches toward him from the beds of its planting, that he might water it.
verses.after: “‘But there was another great eagle, with great wings and plentiful plumage. This vine bent its roots toward him and sent its branches toward him from the beds where it was planted, so that he might water it.
verses.tsw_comparator: But there was another great eagle with great wings and many feathers, and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him, and sent out its branches toward him from the beds of its planting, that he might water it.

verses.rationale: Keeps potential flourishing and repeated water.
verses.before: It was planted in a good field beside abundant waters, to bring forth branches and to bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.'
verses.after: It had been planted in good soil beside abundant water, to put out branches and bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.’
verses.tsw_comparator: It was planted in a good field beside abundant waters, to bring forth branches and to bear fruit, to become a splendid vine.'

verses.rationale: Keeps questions and minimal force required; first eagle remains contextual agent.
verses.before: "Say, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers? All its sprouting leaves will wither, and not by a mighty arm or by many people will it be lifted up from its roots.
verses.after: “Say, ‘This is what the Lord GOD says: Will it thrive? Will he not tear up its roots, strip its fruit, and make all its fresh leaves wither? No great arm or mighty host will be needed to uproot it.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Say, 'Thus says the LORD GOD: Will it thrive? Will he not pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers? All its sprouting leaves will wither, and not by a mighty arm or by many people will it be lifted up from its roots.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated thrive/wither and exact growing location.
verses.before: And look, it is planted. Will it thrive? Will it not utterly wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither on the beds where it sprouted.'"
verses.after: Though it is planted, will it thrive? When the east wind strikes it, will it not wither completely? In the very beds where it grew, it will wither.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And behold, it is planted. Will it thrive? Will it not utterly wither when the east wind touches it? It will wither on the beds where it sprouted.'"

verses.rationale: Separates interpretation from riddle.
verses.before: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: And the word of the LORD came to me, saying,

verses.rationale: Keeps interpretation’s named king and captives without importing personal names.
verses.before: "Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not understand what these things mean?' Say: 'Look, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and princes and brought them to him in Babylon.
verses.after: “Say to the rebellious household, ‘Do you not know what these things mean?’ Tell them: The king of Babylon came to Jerusalem, took its king and its officials, and brought them back with him to Babylon.
verses.tsw_comparator: "Say now to the rebellious house, 'Do you not understand what these things mean?' Say: 'Behold, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and princes and brought them to him in Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves oath, covenant, royal descent, and removal of leaders.
verses.before: And he took one from the royal seed and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath; he also took away the mighty of the land,
verses.after: He took someone of royal descent, made a covenant with him, and put him under oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he took one from the royal seed and made a covenant with him, putting him under oath; he also took away the mighty of the land,

verses.rationale: Connects political survival to treaty keeping.
verses.before: that the kingdom might be lowly, not exalting itself, but observing his covenant, it would stand.
verses.after: so that the kingdom would remain lowly and not rise up, and would stand by keeping his covenant.
verses.tsw_comparator: that the kingdom might be lowly, not exalting itself, but observing his covenant, it would stand.

verses.rationale: Keeps triple questions and echo of riddle’s thrive.
verses.before: But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt, that they might give him horses and a large army. Will he thrive? Will he who does such things escape? Can he break the covenant and escape?
verses.after: But the king rebelled against him, sending envoys to Egypt to obtain horses and a large army. Will he thrive? Will someone who does this escape? Can he break a covenant and escape?
verses.tsw_comparator: But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt, that they might give him horses and a large army. Will he thrive? Will he who does such things escape? Can he break the covenant and escape?

verses.rationale: Keeps intertwined kings and reason for announced death.
verses.before: As I live," declares the LORD GOD, "surely in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, he will die in Babylon.
verses.after: As I live, declares the Lord GOD, he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke.
verses.tsw_comparator: As I live," declares the LORD GOD, "surely in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, he shall die in Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pharaoh’s failed help and siege’s human cost.
verses.before: Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in war, casting up a siege mound and building a siege wall to cut off many lives.
verses.after: Pharaoh with his great army and mighty host will do nothing for him in the war, when siege ramps are piled up and siegeworks built to cut off many lives.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pharaoh with his mighty army and great company will not help him in war, casting up a siege mound and building a siege wall to cut off many lives.

verses.rationale: Keeps hand pledge and repeated no escape.
verses.before: He despised the oath and broke the covenant—although he gave his hand, yet he did all these things—he will not escape.
verses.after: He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. He gave his hand in pledge, yet did all these things. He will not escape.
verses.tsw_comparator: He despised the oath and broke the covenant—although he gave his hand, yet he did all these things—he shall not escape.

verses.rationale: Preserves shift to God’s oath and covenant, not merely the human treaty.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD GOD: As I live, surely my oath which he despised and my covenant which he broke, I will return it upon his own head.
verses.after: “Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: As I live, I will bring down on his head my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD GOD: As I live, surely my oath which he despised and my covenant which he broke, I will return it upon his own head.

verses.rationale: Keeps net/snare parallel with 12:13 and divine litigation.
verses.before: I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there, for the trespass he has committed against me.
verses.after: I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for his unfaithfulness to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there, for the trespass he has committed against me.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned fugitives rather than variant choice troops.
verses.before: All his fugitives and his forces will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to all the winds. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.'"
verses.after: All the fugitives from all his troops will fall by the sword, and those who remain will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.
verses.tsw_comparator: All his fugitives and his forces will fall by the sword, and the survivors will be scattered to all the winds. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.'"

verses.rationale: Keeps God’s direct action and return of cedar shoot image.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD GOD: "I will also take of the lofty top of the cedar and will set it; I will pluck from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.
verses.after: “This is what the Lord GOD says: I myself will take a shoot from the top of the lofty cedar and set it out. From the highest of its young shoots I will pluck a tender one and plant it on a high and towering mountain.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD GOD: "I will also take of the lofty top of the cedar and will set it; I will pluck from the topmost of its young twigs a tender one, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves two bird expressions and repeated dwelling without named political fulfillment.
verses.before: On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, that it may bear branches and produce fruit, and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will dwell under it; they will dwell in the shade of its branches.
verses.after: On Israel’s high mountain I will plant it. It will put out branches, bear fruit, and become a splendid cedar. Every kind of bird, every winged creature, will dwell beneath it; they will dwell in the shade of its branches.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, that it may bear branches and produce fruit, and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will dwell under it; they will dwell in the shade of its branches.

verses.rationale: Keeps both reversal pairs and divine commitment without interpreting the trees individually.
